text:
Alex Johnson  
Tech Lead | NexaCorp | 2 years of experience  
Education: Computer Science, MIT (2022)  

As a results-driven tech lead at NexaCorp, I’ve consistently delivered high-impact solutions in a SaaS environment, leveraging my expertise in cloud-native systems, scalable backend architectures, and cross-functional collaboration. My career began as a Software Engineer Intern at ScaleTech, where I architected a microservices-based pricing engine achieving 95% uptime and reduced deployment time by 40% through optimized CI/CD pipelines. This experience solidified my ability to design systems with measurable reliability and efficiency, a skill I’ve applied across my roles.  

At NexaCorp, I transitioned from Senior Software Engineer to Junior Tech Lead, driving critical projects that scaled our SaaS product to 200k+ active users. As a backend developer, I spearheaded the migration of a monolithic architecture to a serverless model, cutting annual operational costs by $150k while improving scalability. This required deep expertise in cloud infrastructure, particularly AWS services, and demonstrated my ability to balance technical complexity with business outcomes. My work on cloud-native systems included designing a architecture with a 99.95% SLA, integrating advanced monitoring tools like Prometheus and Grafana to ensure real-time visibility into system performance.  

Collaboration has always been central to my approach. As a Tech Lead, I implemented a cross-team collaboration framework that reduced sprint cycle time by 30%, streamlining workflows between product, QA, and DevOps teams. This involved refining Agile/Scrum practices to align with our small team’s needs, ensuring transparency and rapid feedback loops. My stakeholder communication skills were critical in aligning technical roadmaps with business goals, particularly during the serverless migration, where I translated technical constraints into actionable plans for non-technical leadership.  

My proficiency in automation tools like GitHub Actions has been a cornerstone of my productivity. At ScaleTech, I automated 80% of deployment workflows, while at NexaCorp, I extended this to include dynamic environment configurations, reducing manual errors by 65%. Shell scripting has enabled me to create custom tools for log analysis and system diagnostics, further enhancing operational efficiency. Linux administration skills have been vital in maintaining secure, high-performance servers, with a focus on optimizing resource allocation and ensuring compliance with security protocols.  

Database optimization is another area where I’ve made significant contributions. During my time at NexaCorp, I redesigned a PostgreSQL schema to reduce query latency by 50%, using indexing strategies and query caching. This required a deep understanding of data flow and performance bottlenecks, paired with rigorous testing to validate improvements. My technical writing skills are reflected in the documentation I’ve produced for internal systems, which has reduced onboarding time for new engineers by 40%.  

Beyond technical skills, I’ve consistently demonstrated ownership of complex problems. For example, I led the design of a monitoring & alerting system that slashed incident resolution time by 70%, integrating tools like Datadog and Slack for real-time notifications. This required balancing system reliability with alert fatigue, a challenge I resolved through intelligent threshold tuning. My ability to combine technical rigor with business acumen has positioned me as a key contributor to NexaCorp’s growth, and I’m eager to bring this same impact to new challenges.
